remarks: Excellent workmanship. In very good condition, quite playable.  According to Raquet and Martius 2007, probably only the bell section is actually from Drewelwecz’s workshop. The inner slide currently associated with the instrument is by Anton Schnitzer the Elder, the outer slide, by an unknow maker. Flat slide stays, one flat bell stay with eyelet off-center to bell-pipe side; ring in slide-bow. 12 ferrules; some have dragon-scale pattern in middle section; others have similar middle section, with wreath of hammered strokes on one end; still others are similarly decorated, but have a border with pointed teeth and round bows; still others have the wreath of hammered strokes and the same border as the previous group. Bell sleeve has engraved leaf pattern.  Flat bell-stay with engraving of a dog chasing a hare; stylized leaf-like ornaments in corners of bell-stay. Slide bow has ring mounted on plate; bell bow probably originally had ring and plate. Rings and hinge plate adjacent to bell stay have engraved storke pattern. Modest bell flare. Garland with cast leaf pattern. Signature and date on hatched background.
